text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 10.65% over two weeks, with today's small decline continuing a sharp downturn that started November 3rd. The primary driver has been crude oil prices: US oil dropped from the $120s range (implied by the stock's prior strength) to $99.64 per barrel as Trump administration comments—particularly Monday's claim that Iran is "militarily effectively over" and the conflict will end "fairly soon"—triggered expectations of reduced geopolitical risk and lower energy prices. Refiners like Marathon profit when crude is expensive relative to the refined products they sell (gasoline and diesel), so falling oil prices compress those margins and hurt profitability.

The broader context is mixed signals on what comes next. While Trump's rhetoric has pushed oil down on hopes of de-escalation, Secretary of State Rubio simultaneously said Iran negotiations remain "unproductive" with "outrageous" demands, suggesting peace is far from certain. Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity and storage levels are normal, so the weakness isn't about operational problems—it's purely the oil price outlook. If geopolitical tension flares again or Trump's optimism proves premature, crude could rebound and help refiners recover.
